title: Cost Management

header.html: Describe factors that can affect costs in Azure; Explore the pricing calculator; Describe cost management capabilities in Azure; Describe the purpose of tags
the official AZ-900 study guide, skills measured as of July 20, 2026

html:
1Factors that affect costs

Azure follows the consumption-based model (Module 1), so the bill depends on what you deploy and use. [Verify live] for prices.

Factor How it changes the cost
Resource type Each service has its own meters (VM hours, GB stored, operations); the size, tier and SKU matter
Consumption The more you use, the more you pay; stopping or deleting resources stops the charges (a stopped VM that is deallocated stops compute charges, but its disks still cost)
Region (location) The same service can have different prices in different regions
Bandwidth Inbound data is generally free; outbound data (to the internet or between regions) is charged
Subscription and account type A free account, pay-as-you-go, an enterprise agreement and others have different rates and offers
Maintenance and operations Management, monitoring and support plans add cost; software licenses add cost unless you bring your own
Azure Marketplace Third-party products from the Marketplace have their own prices

Ways to reduce cost

Option What it does
Reservations (reserved instances) Commit to one or three years of use for certain resources to get a lower price
Azure savings plan for compute Commit to a fixed hourly spend for one or three years for a discount across compute services
Azure Hybrid Benefit Use existing Windows Server or SQL Server licenses (with Software Assurance) on Azure to pay less
Spot virtual machines Use unused capacity at a big discount, but Azure can evict the VM; good for interruptible work
Right-sizing and autoscaling Use the smallest size that works and scale down when idle
Azure Advisor (Module 14) Gives cost recommendations such as removing idle resources
Exam tip

. "Commit for 1 or 3 years to save" → reservation (or savings plan). "Use my existing Windows Server license" → Azure Hybrid Benefit. "Cheap but can be interrupted" → Spot VM. "Free in, charged out" → bandwidth.

2The pricing calculator

The Azure pricing calculator is a free web tool that estimates the cost of Azure services before you deploy.

  • Choose products, then set region, size, tier and quantity to see a monthly estimate.
  • You can compare options and export or share the estimate.
  • You can use it to plan before you buy; it does not need a deployed resource. [Verify live]
  • It estimates new deployments. For existing resources, use Cost Management (below).

A related tool, the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) calculator, compares the cost of running workloads on-premises versus Azure over a period. Beyond the study guide

Exam tip

. Estimate a future deployment → pricing calculator. Compare on-premises to Azure → TCO calculator. See what you are spending now → Cost Management.

3Microsoft Cost Management

Microsoft Cost Management (in the Azure portal) helps you monitor, allocate and optimize your Azure costs.

Capability What it does
Cost analysis View and break down actual costs by resource, resource group, tag, service or time
Budgets Set a spending limit for a scope and get alerts when it is near or reached
Alerts Notifications for budgets, credit, and anomalies
Recommendations Suggestions to cut cost, such as right-sizing (shown with Azure Advisor)
Exports Send cost data on a schedule to storage for reporting
Scopes Analyze at management group, subscription or resource group level

A budget sends alerts but does not stop resources by default. Beyond the study guide

Exam tip

. "Set a spending limit and be notified" → budget with alerts. "See which resource group costs most" → cost analysis.

4Tags

A tag is a name-value pair you attach to resources, resource groups or subscriptions to organize them. Example: Environment: Production, CostCenter: 1042.

Use tags to:

  • Allocate and report costs by department, project or environment (cost analysis can group by tag).
  • Organize and find resources and automate operations.
  • Apply governance (such as owner and purpose).

Key facts:

  • Tags are not inherited by default: a tag on a resource group does not automatically apply to its resources. Azure Policy can require a tag or copy it from the group.
  • You can have many tags per resource (a limit applies), and the same tag on many resources.
  • Tags are metadata only: they do not change how a resource works.
Exam tip

. "Group costs by department" → tags. "Tags on the resource group apply to its resources automatically" → false (unless Azure Policy does it).

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to estimate the monthly cost of a planned deployment before creating anything. Which tool should it use?

  • AThe Azure pricing calculator
  • BAzure Advisor
  • CAzure Policy
  • DMicrosoft Entra ID
Show the answer

Answer: A. The pricing calculator estimates costs for planned services without deployment.

S2The finance team wants to see the costs of each department's resources in one report. What should be applied to the resources?

  • AResource locks
  • BAvailability zones
  • CPrivate endpoints
  • DTags such as Department
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tags let cost analysis group and allocate cost by department.

S3A company runs a steady workload for three years and wants a lower price in return for a commitment. What fits?

  • ASpot virtual machines
  • BReservations
  • CA free account
  • DPay-as-you-go
Show the answer

Answer: B. A one- or three-year reservation gives a lower price for committed use.

S4Which statement about tags is true?

  • ATags on a resource group are automatically inherited by its resources
  • BTags change the performance of a resource
  • CA resource can have only one tag
  • DTags are name-value pairs used to organize resources and track cost
Show the answer

Answer: D. Tags are metadata. They are not inherited by default and do not affect performance.

S5An organization wants to receive an alert when its monthly Azure spending reaches 80% of the planned amount. What should it create?

  • AA budget with alerts in Cost Management
  • BA resource lock on the subscription
  • CA virtual network peering with another region
  • DA management group for the finance team
Show the answer

Answer: A. Budgets in Cost Management send alerts at chosen thresholds.

S6A company already owns Windows Server licenses and wants to reduce the cost of Windows VMs on Azure. What fits?

  • AAzure Hybrid Benefit
  • BSpot virtual machines
  • CExpressRoute
  • DAzure DNS
Show the answer

Answer: A. Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you use existing eligible licenses on Azure.

S7Which data transfer is generally free in Azure?

  • AInbound data to Azure
  • BOutbound data to the internet
  • CData between regions
  • DAll data transfer
Show the answer

Answer: A. Inbound is generally free; outbound and cross-region transfers are charged.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which factors affect Azure cost? Name three.

Show the answer

Resource type, consumption, region, bandwidth, subscription type, Marketplace products.

R2What does the pricing calculator do?

Show the answer

Estimates the cost of planned Azure services before deployment.

R3Which tool analyzes actual costs and sets budgets?

Show the answer

Microsoft Cost Management.

R4What is a tag?

Show the answer

A name-value pair attached to a resource, group or subscription for organization and cost tracking.

R5Are tags inherited from the resource group by default?

Show the answer

No.

R6Which option uses spare capacity at a discount but can be evicted?

Show the answer

Spot virtual machines.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Cost factors resource type and size, consumption, region, bandwidth (out is charged, in is free), subscription type, Marketplace
Save money reservations and savings plans (1 or 3 years), Hybrid Benefit, Spot VMs, right-size, Advisor
Pricing calculator estimate a planned deployment before you create anything
Cost Management analysis, budgets and alerts, recommendations, exports
Tags name-value pairs for cost allocation and organization; not inherited by default; Azure Policy can enforce
